findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime order keys
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` treats every order key as numeric by calling `math.floor`/`math.ceil`. The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so any non-empty optimized page calls `math.floor(datetime)` and raises `TypeError`, returning 500. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw integer cursor value instead of a datetime, so subsequent pages would compare a timestamp column to an integer. The optimized audit-log path is unusable.

findings.title: Negative-offset pagination slices a Django QuerySet with a negative index
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and the cursor offset is negative, this branch passes a negative start index to a Django QuerySet slice. Django rejects negative slicing with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`; the comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is incorrect. `stop = start_offset + limit + extra` also becomes a nonsensical bound when `start_offset` is negative. A caller can therefore trigger a 500 simply by supplying a cursor with a negative offset.

findings.title: Changing span-buffer keys from sets to sorted sets breaks rolling deploys
findings.body: Existing `span-buf:s:*` keys in Redis were written as sets by the previous `SADD`/`SSCAN` implementation. After a rolling deploy those keys can remain for the Redis TTL (default 3600s) and are still referenced by the flush queue, but the new code performs `ZADD` here and `ZSCAN`/`ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE` elsewhere on them. Redis raises `WRONGTYPE Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value`, so consumers and flushers fail and buffered spans can be lost. This needs a versioned key prefix, backward-compatible handling, or draining the buffer before deploy.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE default SUM corrupts eviction scores for duplicate spans
findings.body: `ZUNIONSTORE` without an aggregate uses `SUM`. Span processing is at-least-once, so after a span has been merged into a parent set, a retry can re-add the same payload to the source key; when the sets are merged again the member exists in both destination and source and its score is doubled. The score is `end_timestamp_precise`, so the `ZPOPMIN` eviction ordering is corrupted (an old span can look newer and survive eviction). The merge should preserve the original timestamp, e.g. with `AGGREGATE MAX`.

findings.title: Eviction cap hardcodes 1000 and ignores max_segment_spans
findings.body: The new eviction limit is hard-coded to 1000, while `SpansBuffer` still accepts `max_segment_spans` (default 1001) but no longer uses it. Deployments that configure a different limit are silently ignored, and spans beyond 1000 are dropped without any metric or log because the previous `segment_span_count_exceeded` signal was removed. This changes the configured data-loss boundary without visibility.

findings.title: Redirect loop cap lowered to 1000 can misroute deep traces
findings.body: The redirect-resolution loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations and the comment documenting the depth limitation was removed. For a project/trace chain longer than 1000 parent links, the loop stops at an intermediate span and writes the redirect to the wrong set, so spans can be merged into the wrong segment or split across segments. The redirect hash is not bounded by the 1000-span eviction cap until flush.

findings.title: No test exercises the new eviction behavior
findings.body: All test changes only add the new required `end_timestamp_precise` field to existing fixtures. There is no test that inserts more than 1000 spans to exercise the new `ZPOPMIN` cap, verifies that the oldest spans are evicted, or checks sorted-set merge behavior for duplicate payloads/scores. The main behavior added by this PR is therefore untested.
